items.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000
items.q: Like I was a sideman for a while at Nick’s playing, as I said with Muggsy Spanier, Pee Wee Irwin, Jimmy McPartland, Miff Mole.

ctx.x: So you’d get a gig — when you went to a club to get a gig, did you have an actual band in mind or did you get the gig and then find the musicians to do it? © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

I usually did what you just said, Monk, I got the gig and then I was able to pick up the musicians to do it. Like I was a sideman for a while at Nick’s playing, as I said with Muggsy Spanier, Pee Wee Irwin, Jimmy McPartland, Miff Mole. And then they asked me to bring a band in, a Dixieland band. And I was the last band to play Nick’s. I was proud to say I had the opportunity to go in there with my own band just before they went out of business, after being in business like 50 years. Then it became a place called…
Everybody that you would call would be expected to know a certain repertoire of tunes at that time?
